message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large.  It is commonly quoted as the **Shannon number**, which is roughly

\[
N \approx 10^{43}\text{–}10^{46}
\]

(about 1 × 10^43 to 1 × 10^46).  This estimate comes from counting all possible ways the pieces can be arranged on the board while respecting the rules of chess (e.g., pawn placement, castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, etc.).  In practice, the exact count is still an open problem, but the consensus is that the number of legal positions is on the order of 10^43 to 10^46.
